SpamWise support

Publication draft · Contact Tim Morgan

SpamWise is a free macOS 27 application for Apple Mail. Optional external model usage is billed by the provider. Public distribution is still being prepared. There is no published download or App Store listing to link yet.

Getting started

  1. Open SpamWise and complete its setup, and allow SpamWise to control Mail when macOS asks.
  2. Start with dry run enabled. Choose an available on-device model or configure an explicit provider. Enter API keys only in SpamWise, where they are saved in Keychain; grant mail-sharing permission separately for a remote provider.
  3. Use Account settings to connect Mail; the check validates each account’s Inbox and Junk mailboxes without changing mail. Keep dry run on until you have reviewed its results, then turn it off in General and confirm.
  4. Inspect Activity. Decisions, attempted mail actions and action failures are separate. Confidence thresholds are provisional and do not promise a particular accuracy rate.

SpamWise and Mail must remain running for monitoring. Closing SpamWise’s windows leaves its menu-bar app running; quitting stops its monitor. Launch at login is optional in General settings. Screen lock and sleep/wake acceptance remain under test; no immediate-delivery guarantee is made.

If mail is not being classified

Check Pause, account inclusion, the selected provider and mail-sharing permission. Contacts, reply history and Good corrections let mail skip classification only in accounts whose trusted receiving servers are configured, so that the sender's authentication can be checked; otherwise they count only as evidence for the model. Open Accounts and scan health for the last successful scan or reported failure. Unreadable mail stays in place while later readable messages can be processed. Permission failures and timeouts leave mail untouched. In System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation, check SpamWise’s Mail permission. Contacts access is optional and is separate from Mail access.

SpamWise filters by scanning each account's Inbox through Mail; large or changing mailboxes may take several sweeps. Enabling SpamWise in Mail's extension settings is not required. See the tested compatibility matrix.

Correcting a decision

Use the Activity inspector or SpamWise’s menu-bar commands for selected Mail messages. Ordinary corrections create address rules. Choose domain scope explicitly when you intend to affect a whole domain. Address rules take precedence over domain rules and relationship trust. A saved correction can remain in effect even if its mail action fails; check the displayed action outcome.

Review Junk provides a bounded, read-only list until you explicitly choose to restore a message. Junk membership alone is not treated as a human training label. SpamWise never deletes messages. If another filter or server rule moves mail again, inspect that filter’s configuration; a confirmed client-side move is not a promise that a server will leave the message there.

Provider and cost problems

A missing key, rate limit, unavailable model, refusal or timeout leaves a message unclassified. SpamWise does not silently choose another provider. Check the selected provider’s account, billing and limits. Never email an API key, password or recovery key to support. Usage costs are estimates; conservative budget reservations can exceed billed usage. Dry run does not disable paid model requests.

See privacy before allowing cloud processing. Gemini’s unpaid terms require particular care for personal mail. The on-device option’s current quality is not established as a replacement for a trained spam detector.

Reporting a problem

Email tim@tim.codes with the SpamWise version, macOS version, account provider, the steps you took, the expected result and the displayed error. Use a synthetic message where possible. Share a redacted diagnostic export if it helps, after reviewing it. Avoid sending real message source or screenshots that expose other mail unless necessary and deliberately chosen.

For upgrades, recovery, login-item removal and optional data removal, follow the lifecycle guide. Back up learning before replacing a build, and keep the recovery key separately. Removing SpamWise must not involve deleting Mail’s databases, mailboxes or containers.
